picks.$comment: The three picks every cell yields, and what each is for (the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-05, docs/ROSTER.md section Rulings of 2026-10-05 -- the registry rebalance). COST BASIS: between deep-tier aliases that lose nothing material on the job, comparable costPerTask observations (same task set, effort and applicable price regime) decide the cost tie before list price. When task methods or price regimes differ, or one observation is missing, list price is only a stated proxy assuming equal input/output volumes; the per-task estimate and range remain unestimated until representative tasks are measured (ECON-8). A frontier benchmark never promotes an alias into a deep-tier cell. The stored routing cells remain the approved ordering: new evidence or a price step requires a registry PR, never an automatic reorder. The cell keys stay `winner` and `runnerUp` because nen direct resolve reads those; this block fixes their meaning. One more word of the verb's is fixed here: `mismatch.compares[].recommended` in the resolve document is the PRIMARY's value (the verb's word predates the three picks); its rename is zheref/nen#389.
picks.fallback: the cell's `runnerUp`: the cost-aligned second best on a DIFFERENT provider or surface (`fallbackRule`), so the work can move when one pool's funds, credits or quota run out. A reviewer alias in that position resolves through its `also`. A quota-only outage may also use picks.inPool's same-provider, same-surface substitute when its own quota remains available: report `in-pool: <alias>` beside this row, without replacing the cross-provider fallback or assuming a shared balance. AT THE AGGREGATE (several pairs), the verb's runner-up is the fallback when it sits in another pool than the primary; when it shares the primary's pool, the fallback is the highest-precedence alias in another pool among the pairs' winners and runner-ups, named beside the verb's runner-up with the word `aggregate` -- derived by the reader from the resolve document until the verb applies the rule (zheref/nen#389).

inPool.$comment: Quota-only substitutes, not routing-cell runner-ups. Each is a distinct actionable alias on the same provider and surface; its separate availability/quota must be read before use. Neither this map nor served metadata changes nen direct resolve or the cross-provider fallback.
